title: What Is Cloud Computing?
description: Understand cloud computing basics, deployment models, and the shared responsibility model.

data.text: Cloud computing means using remote servers hosted on the internet to store, manage, and process data instead of running everything on your own local computer or physical data center. Think of it like electricity: you do not build a power plant to run your laptop; you simply plug into the grid and pay for what you use.

data.title: A Simple Analogy
data.text: If building your own server is like buying a house, cloud computing is like renting an apartment. Someone else maintains the building, pays the utilities, and fixes the roof. You simply move in and use the space you need.
Cloud providers offer services at different levels. The three most common models are Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS).

rows: Runtime, middleware, OS, servers, storage, networking

data.text: Organizations also choose how to deploy their cloud infrastructure. The three main deployment models are public, private, and hybrid cloud.

data.title: Deployment Models
items: Public Cloud — AWS owns and operates the infrastructure. You share hardware with other customers but keep your data logically separated. This is the most common model.
Private Cloud — Your organization runs its own cloud infrastructure, either on-premises or in a dedicated data center. You have full control over hardware and security.
Hybrid Cloud — A combination of public and private clouds. You run sensitive workloads privately and use the public cloud for everything else.

data.text: Security in the cloud is a partnership between you and AWS. AWS is responsible for the security of the cloud — the physical hardware, data centers, and global infrastructure. You are responsible for security in the cloud — your data, identity management, and operating system settings.

terms.definition: Delivery of computing services over the internet, including servers, storage, databases, networking, and software.
Infrastructure as a Service — provides virtualized computing resources over the internet.
Platform as a Service — provides a platform that lets customers develop, run, and manage applications without building infrastructure.
Software as a Service — delivers fully functional software applications over the internet.

data.title: Cloud Service Models in Practice
data.content: A company building a new website might use EC2 (IaaS) to have full control over the server OS. A startup building a web app might use Elastic Beanstalk (PaaS) to avoid managing servers. A marketing team might use Amazon WorkMail (SaaS) just to send and receive email.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cloud computing delivers IT resources over the internet on demand
IaaS gives you the most control; SaaS requires the least management
Public, private, and hybrid clouds serve different organizational needs
AWS manages the physical infrastructure; you manage your data and access
data.takeaway: Next, you will explore how AWS organizes its massive global network of data centers.
